sections.html:
Indiana's northwest corner belongs to Lake County, a Lake Michigan shoreline county that is part of metro Chicago. Crown Point holds the courthouse. Nineteen cities and towns and 11 townships make up the county, home to 498,700 people in 2020, the second-highest count in the state. Hammond has the most residents at 77,879, while Gary covers the most land.

Steel built the older neighborhoods. Inland Steel started in East Chicago in 1903 and Gary Works followed in 1906. The county peaked at 546,253 people in 1970, and steel jobs shrank from more than 60,000 in the 1960s to roughly 18,000 by 2015. Housing now varies sharply block by block. Crown Point keeps growing while Gary struggles with vacancy, yet both are taxed from the same county rolls. People who inherit or hold damaged houses in the older areas are the ones most likely to ask about selling as-is.

Your school district is part of your tax rate, which is why identical assessed values can yield different bills in Hammond, Gary and Crown Point. Crown Point Community School Corporation covers Center Township, and Merrillville Community School Corporation covers Ross Township.

Expect cold, snowy winters, with extra lake-effect snow near the shore: 39.46 inches of precipitation and 29.3 inches of snow in a typical year, and January lows averaging 14.4 degrees. Thunderstorms show up on 40 to 50 days. Repeated freezing and thawing punishes roofs, gutters and old pipes, so postponed upkeep is easy to spot. Selling for cash spares you the repairs a mortgage buyer's lender might insist on.

sections.h2: Where to pay and who to call
sections.html:
Pay at any of three treasurer counters, all open weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The Auditor works out of the Crown Point government building.

OfficeAddressPhone
Treasurer, Crown Point2293 N. Main St., Building A, 2nd Floor219-755-3760
Treasurer, Hammond232 Russell St.219-933-2900
Treasurer, Gary400 Broadway219-881-6300
Auditor, Crown Point2293 N. Main St., Building A, 2nd Floor219-755-3120

Mailing address changes and the deduction filing portal belong to the Auditor. Assessment questions go to (219) 755-3718. The Lake County Treasurer page has the tax search and payment links.

Pick the counter closest to the house you are selling. A Gary owner can pay at 400 Broadway, a Hammond owner at 232 Russell St., and anyone can use Crown Point. Call ahead to confirm which payment types each counter takes, and save yourself a trip across the county. Bring your parcel number and your most recent tax statement, and ask for a printed balance if the title company needs one.

Calumet, Center, Hobart, Ross and St. John townships get no Form 11 mailing for 2026. For them the tax bill serves as the notice, and the appeal deadline is June 15, 2027.

Each of those townships has its own assessor line: Calumet (219) 885-0555, Center (219) 663-0841, Hobart (219) 942-7878, Ross (219) 769-7667 and St. John (219) 365-2777. If your house is in another Lake County township, call the county number to find out which notice applies.

sections.h2: The 2025 state law and your deductions
sections.html:
The standard homestead deduction is $48,000 for taxes payable in 2026, then $40,000 for 2027 and $30,000 for 2028. Offsetting that, the supplemental deduction climbs from 40% to 46% to 52% across those years. Homesteads that get the standard deduction also receive a new credit, the lesser of 10% of liability or $300, with nothing to file.

Seniors now get a credit of up to $150 in place of the old over-65 deduction, subject to income limits of $60,000 single and $70,000 joint. Bill caps hold steady at 1% of gross assessed value for homesteads, 2% for other residential and farm land and 3% for everything else. File deductions through the Auditor's online page.

sections.h2: The tax sale and how to stop it
sections.html:
You can stop a sale only by paying before the cutoff. The county auctions parcels online at zeusauction.com, and they close in batches once bidding opens.

  • The Treasurer must have the amount due in hand by 4:30 p.m. on the day bidding opens, in cash or certified funds, to pull a parcel.
  • Postmarks do not count. Payment must arrive by mail or in person at 2293 N. Main Street.
  • The minimum bid covers delinquent taxes, special assessments, current-year taxes, penalties and a $50 postage and publication amount, plus other sale costs.
  • If a parcel sells above the minimum bid and is never redeemed, the owner of record may be entitled to the surplus.

For certificates sold in 2026, redemption expires September 8, 2027. The cost is 110% of the minimum bid within six months of the sale and 115% after that, plus any excess bid with 5% annual interest. If your parcel sold, read the county's tax sale notice now.

Two installments are due each year, in May and November. Paying up to 30 days late with no earlier delinquency costs 5%. Any later payment costs 10%.

State rules govern appeals. You file Form 130 with the assessing official, attend an informal meeting, and get a county board hearing inside 180 days. Form 131 takes a disagreement to the Indiana Board of Tax Review. This route covers only the current assessment, and a sale, comparable sales or an appraisal can serve as evidence.

Owners who have fallen behind can sell ahead of a scheduled sale, with the balance paid from closing proceeds. Call early, since the cutoff is firm.

  1. Call the Treasurer at 219-755-3760 and ask for the exact amount due, including penalties.
  2. Check the Treasurer's tax sale list to see whether the parcel is on it.
  3. Tell the title company right away if it is, so the payoff and any sale costs are built into the closing.
  4. If your house is in one of the townships with no Form 11 mailing, call the township assessor line to confirm your appeal timing.
  5. Ask the Auditor to update the mailing address for future bills after you close.

A cash buyer can often close before the sale and take the house as it stands, which is useful for inherited or damaged property. The overdue tax and sale costs still come out of your proceeds, and the title company needs the payoff figure in writing. Gather your deed, your latest tax bill and any lien or mortgage payoff letters before you call, so each office can answer in one conversation.

faqs.q: When are Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due in two installments, in May and November. Payments go to the county treasurer.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Lake County property tax in person?
faqs.a: You can pay at the Treasurer's offices in Crown Point, Hammond or Gary, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Did Lake County send assessment notices in 2026?
faqs.a: Not in every township. No Form 11 was mailed for Calumet, Center, Hobart, Ross and St. John, so the tax bill serves as the notice, with a June 15, 2027 appeal date.

faqs.q: How can I find out if my Lake County parcel is in a tax sale?
faqs.a: Check the Treasurer's tax sale list, or call 219-755-3760. The county posts its notice, parcel list and eligibility details on the Treasurer's page.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Lake County house before it goes to a tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, if the closing happens before the deadline to remove the parcel. The balance can be paid from the proceeds, so call early.
